questions.question: If secθ = √2, then cosecθ is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If secθ = √2, then cosecθ is equal to:
questions.solution:
secθ = √2 → cosθ = 1/√2

sinθ = √(1 - cos2θ) = √(1 - (1/√2)2) 

1/√2

cosecθ = 1/sinθ = √2

questions.question: The below figure shows the estimated expenses of a family whose total estimated expenditure was ₹2,50,000. Study the figure and answer the question that follows. It was found that the actual expenditure on electricity was 10% more than the estimated expenditure, and the actual expenditure on rent was 20% less than estimated. All other expenses were same as that of the estimates. What was the total actual expenditure?
questions.questionHtml:
The below figure shows the estimated expenses of a family whose total estimated expenditure was ₹2,50,000. Study the figure and answer the question that follows.

It was found that the actual expenditure on electricity was 10% more than the estimated expenditure, and the actual expenditure on rent was 20% less than estimated. All other expenses were same as that of the estimates. What was the total actual expenditure?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total estimated expenditure = ₹2,50,000

Electricity share = 11%, Rent share = 18%

Actual expenditure on electricity = 10% more than estimated

Actual expenditure on rent = 20% less than estimated

Other expenses remain the same as estimated.

Formula used:

Estimated expense = (Percentage Share) × (Total Estimated Expenditure) ÷ 100

Actual expense = Estimated Expense ± Change

Calculation:

Estimated electricity expense = \(\frac{11 × 250000}{100} = 27500\)

Actual electricity expense = \(27500 + 10\% \text{ of } 27500 = 27500 + 2750 = 30250\)

Estimated rent expense = \(\frac{18 × 250000}{100} = 45000\)

Actual rent expense = \(45000 - 20\% \text{ of } 45000 = 45000 - 9000 = 36000\)

Other expenses = Total estimated expenditure - (Electricity + Rent) = \(\frac{(20 + 16 + 17 + 18)}{100} × 250000 = 177500\)

Total actual expenditure = Electricity + Rent + Other Expenses = \(30250 + 36000 + 177500 = 243750\)

∴ The total actual expenditure is ₹2,43,750.

questions.question: One pipe can fill a tank 6 times faster than another pipe. If both the pipes together can fill the tank in 40 minutes, then in how many minutes will the slower pipe alone be able to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: One pipe can fill a tank 6 times faster than another pipe. If both the pipes together can fill the tank in 40 minutes, then in how many minutes will the slower pipe alone be able to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Let the rate of the slower pipe be x tanks/min.

Faster pipe rate = 6x tanks/min

Combined rate = 7x tanks/min

7x = 1/40

x = 1/280

Time for slower pipe = 1/x = 280 minutes

questions.question: In how much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will ₹10,800 amount to ₹24,800 if invested at simple interest at the rate of 15.5% per annum?
questions.questionHtml: In how much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will ₹10,800 amount to ₹24,800 if invested at simple interest at the rate of 15.5% per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

P = ₹10,800, A = ₹24,800

R = 15.5% p.a.

SI = A - P = 24,800 - 10,800 = ₹14,000

14,000 = 10,800 × 15.5 × T / 100 14,000 = 167,400T / 100

14,000 = 1674T

T = 14,000 / 1674

T ≈ 8.36 Time required

8.36 years

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 80% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 4% votes were declared invalid. A candidate got 15,360 votes which were 80% of the valid votes. Find the total number of votes.
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, 80% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 4% votes were declared invalid. A candidate got 15,360 votes which were 80% of the valid votes. Find the total number of votes.
questions.solution:
Given:

80% of voters cast their votes

4% invalid

15,360 votes = 80% valid votes.

Let total votes be x

0.80x votes cast

0.768x valid votes

15,360 = 0.80 ×  0.768x

x = 15,360 / 0.6144 = 25,000

questions.question: If sin 3A = cos (A - 26º), then A = ______, where 3A is an acute angle.
questions.questionHtml: If sin 3A = cos (A - 26º), then A = ______, where 3A is an acute angle.
questions.solution:
Given sin 3A = cos (A - 26º)

sin θ = cos (90º - θ)

3A = 90º - (A - 26º)

3A + A = 116º

4A = 116º

A = 29º

questions.question: Triangle XYZ is an isosceles triangle with sides XY = XZ. If the measure of angle Y is 80º, what is the measure of angle X?
questions.questionHtml: Triangle XYZ is an isosceles triangle with sides XY = XZ. If the measure of angle Y is 80º, what is the measure of angle X?
questions.solution:
Triangle XYZ is isosceles with XY = XZ

Given angle Y = 80º

Sum of angles = 180ºX + Y + Z = 180º

X + 2(80º) = 180º

X = 20º

questions.question: The given table shows the expenditure (in crore ₹) of three companies A, B, and C and the percentage profit of these companies in different years. Given that: Income = Expenditure + ( Expenditure × Profit % /100 ) Years Company A Expenditure Company A Profit Company B Expenditure Company B Profit Company C Expenditure Company C Profit 2002 24 50% 20 40% 40 45% 2003 30 45% 15 25% 50 55% 2004 36 40% 25 35% 60 65% 2005 40 60% 35 48% 80 75% What is the difference (in crore ₹) between the profits of Company A and Company B in the year 2005?
questions.questionHtml:
The given table shows the expenditure (in crore ₹) of three companies A, B, and C and the percentage profit of these companies in different years. Given that: Income = Expenditure + ( Expenditure × Profit % /100 )

Years Company A Expenditure Company A Profit Company B Expenditure Company B Profit Company C Expenditure Company C Profit
2002 24 50% 20 40% 40 45%
2003 30 45% 15 25% 50 55%
2004 36 40% 25 35% 60 65%
2005 40 60% 35 48% 80 75%

What is the difference (in crore ₹) between the profits of Company A and Company B in the year 2005?
questions.solution:
Given:

Expenditure and profit percentage of Company A and Company B for the year 2005:

Company A: Expenditure = ₹40 crore, Profit% = 60%

Company B: Expenditure = ₹35 crore, Profit% = 48%

Formula for Profit:

\(\text{Profit} = \text{Expenditure} \times \frac{\text{Profit %}}{100}\)

Calculation:

Profit of Company A:

\(\text{Profit}_A = 40 \times \frac{60}{100} = 40 \times 0.6 = 24 \, \text{crore ₹}\)

Profit of Company B:

\(\text{Profit}_B = 35 \times \frac{48}{100} = 35 \times 0.48 = 16.8 \, \text{crore ₹}\)

Difference between profits:

\(\text{Difference} = \text{Profit}_A - \text{Profit}_B = 24 - 16.8 = 7.2 \, \text{crore ₹}\)

∴ The difference between the profits of Company A and Company B in 2005 is ₹7.2 crore.

questions.question: Amit's father is aged five times more than Amit. After 6 years, he would be three and a half times of Amit's age. After further 9 years, how many times of Amit's age would he be?
questions.questionHtml: Amit's father is aged five times more than Amit. After 6 years, he would be three and a half times of Amit's age. After further 9 years, how many times of Amit's age would he be?
questions.solution:
Let Amit's current age = x.

6x + 6 = 3.5(x + 6)

6x + 6 = 3.5x + 21

2.5x = 15 ⇒ x = 6

Amit's age = 6

Father's age = 36

In 15 years: Amit = 21

Father = 51

Times = 51/21 = 17/7 = 2(3/7)

Therefore, after 15 years, Amit's father will be 2(3/7) times Amit's age.

questions.question: In what ratio, sugar costing ₹78 per kg be mixed with sugar costing ₹46 per kg such that by selling the mixture at ₹75 per kg there is a gain of 20%?
questions.questionHtml: In what ratio, sugar costing ₹78 per kg be mixed with sugar costing ₹46 per kg such that by selling the mixture at ₹75 per kg there is a gain of 20%?
questions.solution:
Selling price = ₹75 per kg, Gain = 20%

Cost Price of mixture = ₹75 / 1.20 = ₹62.50 per kg

Using the allegation method:

Quantity ratio = (46 - 62.50) / (62.50 - 78)

= -16.50 / -15.50

 = 33 / 31

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 100 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run before he is over taken?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 100 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run before he is over taken?
questions.solution:
Relative Speed = 23 km/h - 21 km/h = 2 km/h

Convert 2 km/h to m/s: 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s

Time = 100 m / (5/9 m/s) = 180 s

Speed of thief = 21 × (5/18) = 35/6 m/s

Distance = (35/6 m/s) × 180 s = 1050 m

(3x - 2y)2 - 172

questions.question: Find the value of 11 - {(3 ÷ 4) of 8 - (4 - 8)}
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of 11 - {(3 ÷ 4) of 8 - (4 - 8)}
questions.solution:
First, solve the innermost brackets:

4 - 8 = -4

(3 ÷ 4) of 8 = 6

11 - {6 - (-4)} = 11 - 10 = 1

questions.question: The given table shows the percentage of students passing out of college M over five years. Years College M 2018 68 2019 72 2020 40 2021 80 2022 92 What is the percentage increase in the number of students passing out of college M in the year 2022 as compared to the previous year?
questions.questionHtml:
The given table shows the percentage of students passing out of college M over five years.
Years College M
2018 68
2019 72
2020 40
2021 80
2022 92
What is the percentage increase in the number of students passing out of college M in the year 2022 as compared to the previous year?
questions.solution:
Given:

Percentage of students passing out of College M:

2021: 80%

2022: 92%

Formula used:

Percentage Increase = [(New Value - Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100

Calculation:

New Value = 92, Old Value = 80

Percentage Increase = [(92 - 80) ÷ 80] × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = (12 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 15%

∴ The percentage increase in students passing out in 2022 compared to 2021 is 15%.

questions.question: A, B and C invested money in a business such that 2 times A's share, 4 times B's share and 6 times C's share are all equal. If they earned ₹44,000, find the share of A.
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C invested money in a business such that 2 times A's share, 4 times B's share and 6 times C's share are all equal. If they earned ₹44,000, find the share of A.
questions.solution:
Let A's share be a

B's share be b

and C's share be c

b = a/2

c = a/3

a + a/2 + a/3 = 44000

(6a + 3a + 2a)/6 = 44000

11a/6 = 44000

a = 24000

questions.question: Study the given table and answer the question. Year Rice gm/day Wheat gm/day Pulses gm/day Vegetables gm/day 2019 450 55 160 280 2020 430 60 150 300 2021 380 65 140 320 2022 350 70 125 400 2023 350 80 120 350 For which year is the daily consumption equal to that of another given year?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given table and answer the question.
Year Rice gm/day Wheat gm/day Pulses gm/day Vegetables gm/day
2019 450 55 160 280
2020 430 60 150 300
2021 380 65 140 320
2022 350 70 125 400
2023 350 80 120 350
For which year is the daily consumption equal to that of another given year?
questions.solution:
Given:

The table shows daily consumption (in gm/day) of rice, wheat, pulses, and vegetables over five years. We need to find if any two years have equal daily consumption.

Formula used:

Total daily consumption = Rice + Wheat + Pulses + Vegetables

Calculation:

For each year:

2019: 450 + 55 + 160 + 280 = 945 gm/day

2020: 430 + 60 + 150 + 300 = 940 gm/day

2021: 380 + 65 + 140 + 320 = 905 gm/day

2022: 350 + 70 + 125 + 400 = 945 gm/day

2023: 350 + 80 + 120 + 350 = 900 gm/day

The total daily consumption for 2019 and 2022 is the same: 945 gm/day.

∴ The daily consumption in 2022 is equal to that of 2019.

questions.question: The volume of a right circular cylindrical box of radius 30cm is 600cm3. Find the height of the box. ( π = 3.14 )
questions.questionHtml: The volume of a right circular cylindrical box of radius 30cm is 600cm3. Find the height of the box. ( π = 3.14 )
questions.solution:
V = πr2h

600 = π × 302 × h

Solving for h

h = 600 / (900π)

h = 600 / (900 × 3.14)

h ≈ 0.21 cm

questions.questionHtml: PQ is the diameter of a circle with centre A. M is a point on the circumference of the circle. If m∠MAP = 110º, then find the value of m∠MQA.
questions.solution:
∠MAP = 110º

∠MAQ = 180º - 110º = 70º

In ΔMAQ

AQ = AM

∠MQA = ∠QMA = xº

70º + xº + xº = 180º

xº = 55º
